data.hook: Martín Di Nenno's explosive XPLO power, in a softer, arm-friendly package.
why: Geometric head and high balance put real weight behind smashes and vibora
Ease Vibe and Vibradrive soak up to 49% of vibration, so your elbow stays happy
Custom Weight lets you add 3, 6 or 9 g to the tip to tune power
Fibrix face (glass + carbon) over a triple-density Multieva core: soft feel, quick exit
3D Grain rough finish bites the ball for spin and placement
data.playStyle: Attacking players who want big overheads without having to swing at 100%, or anyone coming off a stiff racket who wants more comfort.
data.summary: The XPLO Comfort takes the XPLO family's attacking geometry and pairs it with a softer Fibrix face and multi-density core. You get easy, explosive power from the high balance and a much kinder feel on the arm than the hard XPLO.
data.description:
Bullpadel built the XPLO Comfort for players who want to finish points overhead but don't want a board-stiff racket. The geometric head and high balance give a lot of inertia, so the ball leaves fast even on a three-quarter swing.

The Fibrix face mixes fibreglass and carbon for a softer, more forgiving contact, while the Multieva core layers harder EVA on the outside for speed and a softer layer inside for comfort. Ease Vibe dampers and the Vibradrive handle cut vibration, and the Custom Weight system lets you shift balance to suit your game.

tech.name: Geometric Shape
tech.text: A wider, angular head that adds inertia for more hitting power, especially in the air.

tech.name: Geometric Core
tech.text: Diagonal and vertical supports inside the core reduce twisting on off-centre hits.

tech.name: Hexature
tech.text: Hexagonal tubular frame for rigidity, stability and energy transfer.

tech.name: Air Power
tech.text: A larger channel along the frame for a cleaner, faster swing.

tech.name: Wave System
tech.text: Internal structure that balances flex and stiffness to return more energy.

tech.name: Ease Vibe
tech.text: Dampers built into the face that absorb up to 49% of vibration.

tech.name: Vibradrive
tech.text: Shock-absorbing elastomer in the handle for off-centre hits.

tech.name: Custom Weight
tech.text: Add 3, 6 or 9 g at the tip to fine-tune balance and power.

tech.name: Smart Holes
tech.text: Reinforced drilling pattern that stiffens the face and lifts ball exit.

tech.name: 3D Grain
tech.text: Rough face texture for extra spin and grip on the ball.

faq.q: Who is the XPLO Comfort designed for?
faq.a: Attacking intermediate-to-advanced players who want XPLO-level power with a softer, more comfortable feel.

faq.q: How is it different from the regular XPLO?
faq.a: The Comfort uses a Fibrix (glass + carbon) face and a multi-density core, so it feels softer and easier on the arm, with a little less raw stiffness.
Yes. The Custom Weight system lets you add 3, 6 or 9 g near the tip.
Not ideal. The high balance takes some technique to control. Beginners are better off with a round, low-balance racket.

faq.q: Is it good for players with elbow trouble?
faq.a: It is one of the more comfortable power rackets, thanks to Ease Vibe and Vibradrive, but anyone with an injury should still try it first.

data.clubTake: Brand new, unused. A great step up if you want more punch overhead without the arm buzz of a hard carbon racket.
